strengths: Valuable empirical insight: demonstrates that discussion-based orchestration paradoxically harms SLM performance, with rigorous analysis showing 59.5% of failures due to groupthink
Strong experimental validation across three benchmarks (MATH, GPQA, GSM8K) with appropriate baselines, standard errors, and systematic comparisons
Practical and elegant solution: SLM-MUX is simple, computationally efficient, and effective without requiring costly inter-model communication
Well-motivated model selection search with intuitive two-objective optimization (union accuracy + contradiction penalty) and clear visualization of trade-offs
Clear presentation with informative visualizations, illustrative examples, and promised code for reproducibility
Impressive empirical results: up to 13.4% improvement over baselines, with two SLMs matching/exceeding Qwen 2.5 72B on some benchmarks
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: core method applies existing self-consistency confidence estimation to model selection in a straightforward manner; primarily an application of prior work rather than methodological innovation

Shallow theoretical analysis: binomial distribution argument is intuitive but informal; claims about A(N, p_max) vs A(N, p̄) lack rigorous proof; analysis doesn't explain fundamental architectural reasons why SLMs fail in discussion-based settings

Ad-hoc tie-breaking design using validation set accuracy with no discussion of validation set selection, size requirements, sensitivity to composition, or comparison with alternative tie-breaking strategies

Scalability concerns: model selection search only tested on 5-model pools with 500-sample validation sets; unclear how this scales to much larger candidate pools; exhaustive search may become intractable
Narrow scope: evaluation limited to reasoning benchmarks only (MATH, GPQA, GSM8K); generalization to other task types (translation, summarization, classification) and open-ended generation unclear

Statistical rigor issues: no formal significance tests despite some overlapping confidence intervals; hyperparameter choices (temperature=0.3, k=3, λ=1) lack justification or sensitivity analysis; GPQA and GSM8K gains marginal when considering error bars
Incomplete baselines: missing comparisons with simpler ensemble methods (weighted voting), diversity-aware selection, and approaches beyond discussion-based methods and Agent Forest
Missing ablations: no sensitivity analysis for number of samples per model, temperature, validation set size, alternative tie-breaking strategies, or λ parameter in model selection
Contradiction penalty design is crude and binary; lacks justification for why this specific definition of complementarity is appropriate; no ablation of λ parameter
Limited analysis of failure modes for SLM-MUX itself; acknowledged limitation that 'a model can be very consistent while still being incorrect' deserves deeper investigation

strengths: Important empirical observation that discussion-based orchestration methods harm SLM performance while helping frontier LLMs, providing valuable documentation of a counterintuitive finding
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple model scales (SLMs vs. frontier LLMs) and benchmarks with systematic comparisons to relevant baselines
Clear presentation with effective illustrations of the method workflow and practical results demonstrating that small model ensembles can be competitive
Solid empirical results showing consistent improvements on MATH, GPQA, and GSM8K with detailed reporting of standard errors
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty: The core SLM-MUX method is a straightforward application of self-consistency (Wang et al., 2023) combined with validation-accuracy-based tiebreaking. No learned components or novel aggregation mechanisms are introduced.

Unfair baseline comparisons: Discussion-based methods (MoA, LLM-Debate, MAV) were optimized for frontier models. The paper does not adapt prompts, parameters, or settings for SLMs, making it unclear whether poor performance is inherent or due to suboptimal configuration. No ablations on baseline hyperparameters are provided.

Weak theoretical justification: The mathematical analysis merely notes that A(N, p_max) > A(N, p̄), which is trivial and applies to any ensemble with selection. It does not explain why SLMs specifically suffer from discussion dynamics or characterize conditions for when SLM-MUX should outperform alternatives.

Ad-hoc model selection search: The exhaustive search contradicts the efficiency motivation for SLMs, requires a 500-question validation set, and uses an unmotivated objective function (union accuracy + contradiction penalty with λ=1). Sensitivity to λ and validation set size is not analyzed.

Limited analysis of when/why the method works: Inconsistent compute-scaling behavior across benchmarks (Figure 9) is unexplained. No principled guidance on when to add models vs. samples. Task-dependent performance variations lack analysis. No detailed error analysis provided.

Groupthink validation is insufficient: The claim that discussion methods cause groupthink rests on LLM-assisted classification (unreliable for analyzing LLM behavior) with only ~60% agreement and limited to LLM-Debate, yet claims are generalized to all discussion methods. Alternative explanations (inherent reasoning limitations) are not ruled out.

Critical missing ablations: No ablations on tiebreaker mechanism, confidence metrics, random vs. learned selection, or validation set size effects. These are essential to understand which components drive performance.

Incomplete baseline coverage: Limited comparison with Agent Forest (most relevant baseline). All evaluated benchmarks are mathematical reasoning tasks with no evaluation on classification, QA, or other domains, limiting generalizability claims.

Statistical testing absent: Only standard errors provided; no significance testing despite overlapping confidence intervals (e.g., MATH 61.8±1.2 vs. 58.0±2.2). Multiple comparisons raise multiple comparison correction concerns.

Reproducibility concerns: Temperature differs between main experiments (0.3) and search (0.5) without explanation. Project page redacted; code availability unclear. Implementation details incomplete (prompt formatting, edge cases).

strengths: Clear and well-validated finding that discussion-based orchestration methods fail for SLMs while succeeding for frontier LLMs, demonstrated through systematic evaluation (Section 4.1) and detailed failure analysis showing 59.5% of failures due to groupthink (Appendix C).

Comprehensive experimental validation across three benchmarks (MATH, GPQA, GSM8K) with thorough ablations, standard error reporting, and comparison of both SLMs and frontier LLMs showing scale-dependent behavior.
Practical and training-free method achieving substantial improvements (up to 13.4% over discussion-based methods) and efficiency gains (two SLMs matching or exceeding Qwen 2.5 72B on key benchmarks).
Principled model selection approach with well-motivated two-objective formulation (Union Accuracy vs. Contradiction Penalty) and clear visualization of accuracy-diversity trade-offs (Figure 7).

Excellent presentation with clear figures, well-structured ablations, and effective communication of complex orchestration concepts. Strong theoretical justification through binomial distribution analysis (Section 5).
Detailed analysis of failure modes in discussion-based methods with qualitative examples, making the groupthink phenomenon concrete and interpretable.
weaknesses: Limited core methodological novelty: SLM-MUX is essentially self-consistency (Wang et al. 2023) plus validation accuracy tie-breaking. While the problem identification is valuable, the technical contribution is incremental.

Ad-hoc tie-breaking mechanism using validation accuracy is static and non-adaptive, with coarse-grained resolution (marginal differences in validation accuracy could be noise). More sophisticated confidence estimation beyond self-consistency is needed.

Inconsistent and unexplained scaling behavior: adding models helps MATH but hurts GPQA (peaks at K=2), contradicting union accuracy trends. Paper lacks clear guidance on when to add models vs. samples, and the contradiction penalty doesn't adequately explain these dynamics.

Model selection search scalability limited to exhaustive search over small pools (5 models). Hyperparameter λ requires tuning with no sensitivity analysis provided. Approach doesn't scale to larger model pools.

Heavy dependence on validation set quality/size with minimal discussion: How sensitive are results to validation set characteristics? What is the practical cost of obtaining representative validation data? How to select validation data for new domains?

Limited evaluation scope restricted to reasoning benchmarks (math, QA) on specific model families (Llama, Mistral, Gemma, Qwen). Unclear generalization to coding, summarization, or other task categories. No cross-family orchestration experiments.
Incomplete failure analysis: Paper shows when SLM-MUX helps but lacks discussion of when it underperforms. No analysis of question types or domains where the method consistently fails.

Missing code repository link ("Project page and code: .") and incomplete hyperparameter documentation (temperature settings, λ selection rationale, ablation on number of samples). Harms reproducibility.

Theoretical analysis in Section 5 makes strong simplifying assumptions (independence, constant correctness probability) and doesn't explain the underlying mechanisms of groupthink—provides indirect evidence only.

Comparison fairness concerns: SLM-MUX uses K models with K× inference cost; token usage varies across comparisons; Table 4 allows variable sample counts across methods. Computational cost analysis could be clearer.

strengths: Strong empirical results demonstrating significant improvements over existing orchestration methods (up to 13.4% on MATH, 8.8% on GPQA, 7.0% on GSM8K)
Well-motivated and counterintuitive finding that discussion-based methods harm SLM performance while helping frontier LLMs, with detailed analysis of groupthink failures (59.5% of cases)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation with appropriate baselines, multiple datasets, extensive ablations, and validation studies in appendix
Simple and practical method requiring no training or model retraining, immediately deployable for practitioners
Generalization demonstrated across frontier LLMs, domain-specific fine-tuned models, and open-ended generation tasks
Clear presentation with good visualizations and thorough documentation of experimental details
Achieves impressive practical result: two SLM ensemble outperforms much larger Qwen 2.5 72B on multiple benchmarks
weaknesses: Limited core novelty: self-consistency for confidence estimation is from prior work (Wang et al. 2023); applying it to multi-model selection is relatively straightforward
Method also improves frontier LLM performance (Appendix E.2), undermining the 'SLM-specific' framing and suggesting the contribution is more general than claimed
Model selection search uses ad-hoc contradiction penalty formulation with hyperparameter λ arbitrarily set to 1; exhaustive search doesn't scale to larger model pools
Potential data leakage concern: validation accuracy used as tie-breaker in SLM-MUX, and model selection search performed on validation sets of only 500 questions
Unfair comparison for discussion-based methods in Section 4.1: evaluated with temperature=0 while these methods are designed for temperature > 0 to generate diverse outputs
Groupthink analysis (59.5%) relies on LLM-as-judge classification which could itself be biased; lacks explanation of why SLMs exhibit groupthink more than frontier models
Weak theoretical contribution: Hoeffding bounds are standard concentration inequalities without deep insight into SLM-specific advantages; analysis in D.2 is straightforward
Static routing that doesn't adapt to specific questions; acknowledged limitation with no solution proposed
Limited scope: only reasoning tasks evaluated (math, QA, code); no evaluation on language understanding or other domains
Insufficient design space exploration: only k=3 samples tested, tie-breaking via validation accuracy not well-justified, no query-adaptive variants explored

strengths: Identifies important limitation: orchestration methods for frontier LLMs fail on SLMs due to groupthink (59.5% of failures), a valuable empirical finding
Strong empirical results across multiple benchmarks (up to 13.4% improvement on MATH) with two SLMs matching Qwen 2.5 72B on GPQA/GSM8K
Comprehensive experiments spanning model sizes, generalization to open-ended generation and domain-specific models, with good ablations and consistency-accuracy analysis
Clear algorithm description and reproducibility focus (Algorithm 1, visual examples, promised code release)
Practical value: no retraining required, efficient computation, immediately applicable for practitioners
weaknesses: Critical methodological flaw: inconsistent temperature settings across comparisons (SLM-MUX uses temp=0.3 while baselines use temp=0 in Figure 5). Since self-consistency requires temperature to generate diverse outputs, this confound could explain most performance gains, invalidating core claims

Limited technical novelty: routing via self-consistency is straightforward; self-consistency as confidence signal already exists (Wang et al. 2023). Main contribution is empirical finding rather than algorithmic innovation, insufficient for top-tier venue

Model selection search concerns: uses 500 validation examples (significant dataset portion), hyperparameter λ=1 lacks justification/sensitivity analysis, exhaustive search unscalable despite scalability claims, no comparison with cited model selection work (Chen et al. 2025, Poon et al. 2025)

Weak theoretical analysis: Hoeffding bound in Section 5 is standard and provides limited insight into why routing outperforms discussion; Appendix D.2 comparative analysis is conceptual without formal rigor
Groupthink analysis unverified: LLM-based classification of 59.5% groupthink lacks human ground truth or inter-annotator agreement; inherent subjectivity undermines this key supporting evidence
Static, non-adaptive design acknowledged but not addressed: uses fixed pre-selected models, crude validation-accuracy tie-breaking, and no per-question adaptation despite feasibility
Generalization claims overstate results: frontier LLM gains minimal except GPQA (10pp); ceiling effects underexplored; HumanEval shows modest gains
Missing rigorous comparisons: no weighted ensemble baseline, other confidence estimators not evaluated, no sensitivity analysis for critical hyperparameter λ

strengths: Identifies important negative result: discussion-based orchestration methods harm SLM performance while helping frontier models, with concrete groupthink analysis showing 59.5% of failures attributed to consensus amplification
Strong empirical results across multiple benchmarks (13.4% improvement on MATH over existing methods; 2-SLM ensemble matches Qwen 2.5 72B on GPQA/GSM8K)

Comprehensive and rigorous evaluation with proper baselines (original code/prompts), multiple benchmarks, ablation studies, consistency-accuracy correlation analysis, random selection baselines, and reproducibility details
Practical and simple solution requiring no model training or inter-model communication; immediately deployable
Well-designed model selection search that balances complementary objectives (union accuracy vs. contradiction penalty)
Extensions demonstrate generalization: open-ended generation (HumanEval), frontier LLMs (GPT-4o, Gemini), and domain-specific fine-tuned models
Clear presentation with effective figures, thorough appendix (27 pages), and theoretical grounding via Hoeffding inequality analysis
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: self-consistency-based routing and majority voting for model selection are well-established techniques; core contribution is empirical application to SLMs rather than algorithmic innovation

Model selection search scalability concerns: exhaustive search acknowledged as impractical for large model pools; Table 10-11 show random selection achieves 60-100% of optimal gains, undermining search necessity and value
Static, non-adaptive design: fixed model selection across all queries and simplistic validation-accuracy tie-breaking; no query-adaptive routing despite clear opportunity (e.g., routing by task type)
Incomplete hyperparameter analysis: λ parameter in contradiction penalty only tested at λ=1; sensitivity to N (samples) and temperature not explored; these directly affect accuracy-compute tradeoffs

Computational cost insufficiently analyzed: method requires N×K forward passes but Figure 1 only compares against other multi-model methods, not single-model + self-consistency baseline; practical compute/accuracy comparison missing

Confidence estimation concerns: pure consistency-based confidence vulnerable to overconfident-but-wrong models; contradiction penalty is somewhat ad-hoc; no ablation showing necessity of penalty component
Weaker results on GPQA (4-5% improvement) with limited investigation of why consistency signals are weaker on this benchmark, suggesting domain-dependent limitations
Validation set dependency: method requires validation data for search and tie-breaking; search stability analysis only tested at 100-500 examples; behavior with minimal validation sets unclear
Missing failure analysis: no exploration of edge cases (e.g., correlated model errors, adversarial inputs) or scenarios where consistency-based routing fails
Insufficient complementarity analysis: Figure 4 shows accuracy differences but lacks investigation of *why* models complement each other or what capabilities each contributes
